mechanism_narrative: Sustained negative TRANSIT mobility (-24 to -26 points) indicates suppressed commuting. This depresses retail footfall because workers avoid transit-dependent shopping trips. RETAIL_REC will remain negative over the next four weeks as transit constraint persists.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT averaged -24.8 over last four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -15 points in any week of the next four weeks AND RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases by more than 3 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility (2.0 to 4.0 points) signals increased essential-goods shopping. Consumers making more frequent essential trips will incidentally increase retail-and-recreation visits during the same outings. RETAIL_REC will rise over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 3.5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 4.0 in t-0w, highest in series
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 3.5 for two consecutive weeks in the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows high volatility (t-1w: -25.9, t-0w: -15.7), indicating weather or policy-driven outdoor activity swings. When PARKS recovers sharply, consumers redirect discretionary time from retail to outdoor recreation. RETAIL_REC will decline over the next four weeks if PARKS continues recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered 10.2 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains below -10 points for all four weeks ahead AND RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 points relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility elevation (3.0 to 4.0 points) combined with sustained WORKPLACES suppression (-7.7 to -8.4) indicates remote work persistence and home-based consumption. This reduces retail-and-recreation visits. RETAIL_REC will decline or remain flat over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 3.0 AND WORKPLACES below -7.0 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 3.3 and WORKPLACES at -8.4 in t-0w
failure_condition: Both RESIDENTIAL remains above 3.0 and WORKPLACES remains below -7.0 for three consecutive weeks ahead, yet RETAIL_REC increases by more than 1 point relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT suppression below -23 points signals active mobility restrictions or low confidence in public transport. When TRANSIT falls below this threshold, retail venues dependent on transit access experience reduced foot traffic. RETAIL_REC will remain negative if TRANSIT stays suppressed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -23 points in any week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has not exceeded -23.9 in any of the four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains below -23 points for all four weeks ahead but RETAIL_REC rises above -5 points in any week.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 10.2 points week-on-week in final week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -10 points for two consecutive weeks in the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior four-week mean.
